surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the interaction between oxygen radicals and the Si3N4 surface, leading to the formation of an oxygen-deficient interfacial layer. At low RF power, fewer oxygen radicals are formed, resulting in increased migration of Si and N atoms from Si3N4 to Al2O3. At higher RF power, more oxygen radicals are generated, which suppresses the migration of Si and N atoms, improving the interfacial quality.
evidence: Based on x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and auger electron spectroscopy, an oxygen-deficient interfacial layer was formed for Al2O3 film deposition at 50 W. Increased migrations of Si and N atoms were observed at low power due to the formation of fewer oxygen radicals. While reduced migrations of Si and N atoms from Si3N4 to Al2O3 were observed when the RF power was sufficient due to the sufficient oxygen radicals.
